thread_analysis.thread_summary: [COMPANY]'s previously-registered product had its BLE module discontinued (EOL) and replaced with an alternative module from a different chip vendor, prompting a new Bluetooth SIG registration even though the end product's name and model are unchanged. The thread, spanning quoting through registration completion, covers whether multiple models can be registered at once versus the recommended practice of adding models afterward for free, how to anticipate what a third party will see on the published listing before Submission, what the TCW (Test Coverage Waiver) field means, and how to handle blank Member Detail fields on the registration, closing with payment confirmation, registration finalization, and compliance folder/invoice delivery.
all_questions_found: If a previously-registered product's BLE module becomes EOL and is replaced with an alternative module, even though the product's name and model are unchanged, does this require a brand-new SIG registration?
Is this engagement subject to Japan's subcontracting law (下請け法), and is a separate purchase order required, or can the submitted Invoice serve as the order?
When is the invoice for the registration service issued -- only after SIG certification and compliance folder delivery, or can it be issued earlier if needed for this month's accounting cutoff?
Is a new SIG registration limited to registering only one model, or can multiple models be registered at once, and what is the recommended approach?
What documentation is needed for the registration confirmation form and the compliance folder?
Is there a way to check what fields a third party will see when viewing the published registration listing, before Submission?
What does the TCW field mean, given it shows a specific number rather than a Yes/No value?
Are blank fields such as company City a problem on the registration, and if so, how can they be corrected?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The thread illustrates that a module-level hardware change (an EOL BLE module replaced by an alternative module from a different vendor) requires a new SIG registration even when the end product's branding is unchanged, since the registration is tied to the underlying module/Controller design, not the product's commercial name. It also covers registration-site mechanics: the one-model-minimum (not one-model-maximum) requirement for new registrations, the limited visibility of pre-Submission registration content (Review Page only, versus a Listing Owner's post-Submission early access), using other companies' already-published listings as a reference to infer which fields become publicly visible, the purpose of the TCW (Test Coverage Waiver) mechanism for Inter-Layer Dependencies attributable to SIG's own system, and the auto-populated, non-editable nature of Member Detail fields on the registration.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: A module substitution (even an EOL-driven, like-for-like replacement) changes the underlying Controller/Component design referenced by the registration, so a new registration is required regardless of whether the end product's name or model designation changes. SIG's new-registration requirement is a minimum of one model in the Product List, not a maximum, but because new registration involves substantial additional input and confirmation, and because Product List entry errors can only be requested for deletion (not corrected) by SIG, the practical recommendation is to register the first model at new-registration time and add further models afterward via the free Product-List addition entry point, rather than including multiple models in the initial registration. Pre-Submission, only the Review Page is visible to the registrant; to anticipate what a third party will eventually see, compare another company's already-published listing of a similar registration type against the Review Page's field names. TCW exists specifically to allow Submission despite an unresolved Inter-Layer Dependency when that dependency is attributable to SIG's own system, by entering the relevant TCW number for confirmation and approval. Blank, auto-populated Member Detail fields (sourced from the Member registration database, not editable during product registration) do not block new registration, and underlying data corrections (such as a company address) should be requested directly from the company's Primary Contact in the Member database, not through the registration workflow.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Assuming an EOL module swap doesn't require a new registration because the product name is unchanged would leave the actual shipped hardware uncertified. Attempting to pack multiple models into the initial new registration, rather than adding them afterward via the free addition entry point, risks an uncorrectable Product List entry error, since SIG can only delete (not edit) mis-entered Product List items. Treating blank Member Detail fields as a registration-blocking error, rather than recognizing them as auto-populated and historically harmless, could cause unnecessary delay.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When a customer's underlying Bluetooth module changes -- even an EOL-driven substitution with no change to the end product's branding -- treat it as requiring a new registration, since SIG registration tracks the module/Controller design, not the commercial product name. When a new registration could cover several models, register the first one initially and use the free Product-List addition entry point for the rest, since mis-entered Product List items cannot be corrected, only deleted. To answer a customer's question about public listing visibility, point them to an already-published comparable listing rather than promising a direct preview tool that doesn't exist pre-Submission.
